name: session-sitter
description: Tabbed session switcher for Claude Code, IBM Bob, Codex and VS Code Chat — with traffic-light supervision of the actions your agents pause on

commands.title: Probe Claude Targeting — where a message would land (debug)
Probe Bob Question — full approval state (debug)

enumDescriptions: Recently updated — newest activity first. Rows move as sessions update.
Machine, then workspace, then title. Rows hold still.
Workspace, then title, regardless of machine. Rows hold still.
Agent (Claude, Bob, Codex, Chat), then workspace. Rows hold still.
Session title, A to Z. Rows hold still.
Needs you first: waiting, then running, then idle.
sessionSitter.sessionSort.markdownDescription:
How the **Sessions** list and **History** are ordered. Also switchable from the panel's ⇅ toolbar button, which writes this setting.

`recent` (the default) sorts by newest activity, so rows move every time a session updates — which is what makes it hard to keep your place. The other orders sort by properties of the session rather than by the clock, so a row only moves when a session appears or disappears:

- `hostWorkspace` — machine, then workspace, then title. This machine's sessions lead.
- `workspace` — workspace, then title, regardless of which machine it is on.
- `source` — grouped by agent: Claude, Bob, Codex, Chat.
- `title` — alphabetical by session title.
- `status` — waiting on you first, then running, then idle (newest first inside each group; this one does move).

sessionSitter.workspaceColors.markdownDescription:
Colour for the **workspace pill** on a session row, per workspace. Unlisted workspaces keep the theme's badge colour.

Each key is a workspace **name** (`my-app`), a full workspace **path** (`/home/you/work/my-app`), or a glob over either (`*` = any run of characters, `?` = one; `*` alone matches every workspace). Keys are tried in the order you write them and the **first match wins**, so put a specific workspace above a broad glob.

Each value is a hex colour (`#0f8`, `#1a2b3c`), one of the built-in names — `red`, `orange`, `amber`, `yellow`, `lime`, `green`, `teal`, `cyan`, `blue`, `indigo`, `violet`, `purple`, `magenta`, `pink`, `brown`, `slate`, `gray` — or `auto` to derive a stable colour from the workspace itself. The label colour is chosen for contrast automatically. A value that is not a colour is ignored, leaving that pill on the theme colour.

Example:

```json
{
  "session-sitter": "green",
  "/home/you/work/payments": "#c0392b",
  "scratch-*": "slate",
  "*": "auto"
}
```

sessionSitter.probelessActiveWindowMinut.markdownDescription: How recently a **Codex** or **VS Code Chat** session must have been updated to count as active in the Sessions list. Those sources expose no live-process signal, so recency is the only available proxy; Claude and Bob sessions are judged by what their extension hosts actually report as open. Set to `0` to keep them in History always.

sessionSitter.windowAttentionMinutes.markdownDescription:
How long after someone last interacted with an IDE window that window's report of its open sessions still counts, in minutes. `0` (the default) turns this off, and every live window's report counts however long ago it was last touched.

This exists for remote IDEs. The process that publishes a window's open sessions is the **server-side** extension host, and closing the client window does not stop it: the server keeps it alive for a reconnect, so it goes on reporting the sessions that were open when you disconnected. Setting this makes those reports expire.

Raise it rather than lower it if a session you are working in moves to History too eagerly. Windows running a build of this extension too old to publish the signal are always treated as attended.

sessionSitter.remotePeers.markdownDescription:
Whether to show sessions from other machines. `auto` (default) finds peer machines from the remote windows this IDE has already opened — no configuration needed — and pulls their live sessions over SSH, reusing one connection per peer. Clicking such a session focuses the window on **its own** machine. Set to `off` to disable this entirely: no peer discovery, no polling, and no SSH connection of any kind.

Only peers reachable from this machine appear. SSH runs with `BatchMode=yes`, so a host that would prompt for a password is reported unreachable rather than blocking.

sessionSitter.autoRespond.markdownDescription:
Auto-respond rules for **Bob** and **Claude** sessions, evaluated in order (first match wins). Each rule is either a **text rule** `{ matchPattern, response }` (sends `response` when the latest assistant message matches the `matchPattern` regex) or an **approval rule** `{ toolPattern, decision }` (resolves a pending tool-approval prompt when `toolPattern` — a glob, `*` = any run of characters, `|` = alternatives — matches the tool name, optionally narrowed by an `argumentPattern` regex over the arguments JSON). Set `source` to `bob` (default) or `claude`. Add an optional `sessionPattern` (regex) to scope a rule to sessions whose project path matches.

A pending prompt that no rule handles is left for you — or handed to the supervisor when `sessionSitter.autoSupervise` is on. A user-facing question (`ask_followup_question` / `AskUserQuestion`) is never auto-approved.

sessionPattern.description: Optional: JavaScript regex matched against the session's project path. When set, the rule applies only to sessions whose project path matches; omit to apply to all sessions.

matchPattern.description: Text rule: JavaScript regex tested against the latest assistant message.

response.description: Text rule: text sent into the session on a match.

toolPattern.description: Approval rule: glob matched against the pending tool name ('*' = any run of characters, '|' separates alternatives).

argumentPattern.description: Approval rule (optional): JavaScript regex matched against the pending tool arguments as JSON. Unanchored — matches anywhere in the JSON.

decision.description: Approval rule: how to resolve the prompt. approveForTask also suppresses future prompts for that permission group (and command, for execute_command).

source.description: Which IDE the rule applies to: 'bob' (default) or 'claude'.

sessionSitter.supervisorStateDir.markdownDescription:
Absolute path to the supervision state directory. **Required to enable supervision.** Transcripts are exported to `<stateDir>/history/`, decisions are recorded in `<stateDir>/records/` (what the Supervision activity panel shows), and interventions queue in `<stateDir>/outbox/` until the agent confirms them.

Example: `/home/you/.ai-sessions/state`

sessionSitter.autoSupervise.markdownDescription: When on, every agent prompt that no auto-approve rule handles is handed to the supervisor: the transcript is exported, the action is classified into a traffic light, and the decision is applied back into the agent. Requires `sessionSitter.supervisorStateDir`.

sessionSitter.supervisorRepoPath.markdownDescription: Workspace root the supervisor runs against — used to locate `.env` files and as the classifier's working directory. Derived from `sessionSitter.supervisorStateDir` (its parent) when empty.

sessionSitter.supervisor.engine.markdownDescription: Which agent CLI classifies an ambiguous action: `bob` (IBM Bob Shell, default) or `claude` (Claude Code). The deterministic tier and your `sessionSitter.autoRespond` rules run first and need no CLI at all.

sessionSitter.supervisor.fastClassifier.markdownDescription:
When on, an ambiguous action is first judged by the **fast** classifier: one HTTP call that reuses the agent's own paused conversation as a prompt-cached prefix, so it answers in a few seconds instead of the ten-plus an agent CLI needs. The CLI selected by `sessionSitter.supervisor.engine` stays as the fallback for timeouts, unparsable verdicts and low-confidence answers.

**Requires an API token and a gateway URL, which most Claude Code users do not have.** If you signed in with a Pro/Max/Team subscription, your credentials are held in the OS keychain via OAuth and there is no `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` or `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` to use — so this stays off, and ambiguous actions go to the agent CLI exactly as before. Nothing breaks; it simply has no effect. It applies when you run against an API key or a gateway (see the three settings below).

sessionSitter.supervisor.fastClassifierM.markdownDescription: Model the fast classifier judges with. Empty uses the **agent's own** model (`ANTHROPIC_MODEL`), minus any trailing context-window suffix such as `[1m]` — which a plain Messages endpoint rejects. So by default the supervisor thinks with the same model as the agent it supervises.

sessionSitter.supervisor.fastClassifierT.markdownDescription: How long the fast classifier may take before the action is handed to the agent CLI instead. Keep it short: the point of the tier is that it is fast, and the fallback is what covers the slow tail.

sessionSitter.supervisor.fastClassifierB.markdownDescription: Gateway the fast classifier posts `/v1/messages` to. Empty falls back to `sessionSitter.supervisor.anthropicBaseUrl` (and then to `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`). The token is the one from `sessionSitter.supervisor.anthropicAuthToken` / `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`.

sessionSitter.supervisor.bobCliPath.markdownDescription: Path to the `bob` executable used when `sessionSitter.supervisor.engine` is `bob`.

sessionSitter.supervisor.claudeCliPath.markdownDescription: Path to the `claude` executable used when `sessionSitter.supervisor.engine` is `claude`.

sessionSitter.supervisor.bobApiKey.markdownDescription:
API key for headless Bob classification (passed to the CLI as `BOBSHELL_API_KEY`). Leave empty to fall back to `BOBSHELL_API_KEY` / `BOB_API_KEY` in the environment or a `.env` file.

**Note:** VS Code settings are stored in plain text. Prefer the environment fallback if that matters to you.

sessionSitter.supervisor.anthropicBaseUr.markdownDescription: Optional Claude Code gateway base URL, passed to the classifier subprocess as `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`. Empty falls back to the environment / `.env` value, if any.

sessionSitter.supervisor.anthropicAuthTo.markdownDescription:
Optional auth token for the Claude Code gateway, passed as `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`. Empty falls back to the environment / `.env` value, if any.

**Note:** VS Code settings are stored in plain text.

sessionSitter.supervisor.classifierTimeo.markdownDescription: How long to wait for the classifier CLI before treating the classification as failed.

sessionSitter.supervisor.messagingChanne.markdownDescription: Where decisions and updates go. `telegram` sends real cards (needs the bot token + chat id below); `stub` writes them to `<stateDir>/notifications/` and reads simulated replies from `<stateDir>/inbox/<requestId>.txt`.

sessionSitter.supervisor.telegramBotToke.markdownDescription:
Telegram bot token (from @BotFather), used when `sessionSitter.supervisor.messagingChannel` is `telegram`. Empty falls back to `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` in the environment or a `.env` file.

**Note:** VS Code settings are stored in plain text; use the environment fallback if you would rather not keep the token there.

sessionSitter.supervisor.telegramChatId.markdownDescription: Telegram chat id that receives the cards. Empty falls back to `TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID` in the environment or a `.env` file.

sessionSitter.telegram.remoteControl.markdownDescription:
Turn on the **Telegram remote interface**: your sessions appear as topics in a Telegram forum group, and typing in a session's topic sends that text into the session.

Each session gets its own topic, so the thread you are typing in *is* the session you are talking to. `General` holds the live session list and the `/sessions`, `/new`, `/who` and `/help` commands.

Setup, once:

1. Create a Telegram **group**, open its settings and turn **Topics** on.
2. Create a bot with @BotFather, and **disable privacy mode** for it (`/setprivacy` → Disable) so it can read messages typed in a topic.
3. Add the bot to the group as an admin with **Manage Topics**.
4. Put the bot token in `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` and the group id in `TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID` (environment or a `.env` file), or in `sessionSitter.supervisor.telegramBotToken` / `.telegramChatId`.
5. List the Telegram user ids allowed to drive it in `sessionSitter.telegram.allowedUserIds` — **without this nothing is acted on**.

**Use one bot per machine.** A bot token has a single message stream and reading it is destructive, so two machines sharing a token steal each other's messages. Prefer the environment or a `.env` file over VS Code settings for the token: Settings Sync would copy one machine's token to all of them.

Reading works for Claude, Bob, Codex and Chat sessions. Sending works for Bob, and for Claude sessions open in their own window; Codex and VS Code Chat expose no message API, so their topics are read-only and say so.

sessionSitter.telegram.allowedUserIds.markdownDescription:
Telegram **user ids** permitted to drive the remote interface. **An empty list authorises nobody**, which is the default.

This matters more than it does for supervision cards: a group is not a private chat, so anyone who was ever invited could otherwise send text straight into your coding agents.

To find your id, turn the feature on, send any message in the group, and read the extension's Output log — the id of each rejected sender is logged for you to copy in.

Example:

```json
["123456789"]
```

sessionSitter.telegram.fullMessages.markdownDescription:
Mirror the **whole text** of each turn into its Telegram topic, split across as many messages as it needs.

With this off, a turn is shown as the same short preview the Sessions panel draws beside a session — about 250 characters. That is enough to recognise an answer next to the session it belongs to, and not enough to *act* on one when Telegram is all you have: the part you need in order to reply is usually the end of it.

Telegram caps a message at 4096 characters, so a long answer becomes several messages, numbered `(1/3)`, `(2/3)`, `(3/3)`. Use `sessionSitter.telegram.maxMessageParts` to say how many.

Only the mirror is affected. The panel's preview bubbles are unchanged.

sessionSitter.telegram.maxMessageParts.markdownDescription:
How many Telegram messages one turn may be split into when `#sessionSitter.telegram.fullMessages#` is on. Four covers roughly 16,000 characters.

Anything past the budget is not silently dropped: the last message ends with the exact number of characters left out and points at the **📄 Full transcript** button, which uploads the whole thing as a file.

The ceiling is 20 because that is about what Telegram accepts per minute for one group — a larger budget would let a single long answer hold up every other session's topic. When several turns arrive in the same pass, the budget goes to the **newest** one and the earlier ones get one message each, on the same reasoning: the last turn is the one you are about to answer.

sessionSitter.supervisor.orangeResponseT.markdownDescription: How long an interactive decision card waits for your answer. On timeout, silence is **not** approval: an Orange denies the action and hands the agent safe alternatives; a Red stays blocked.

sessionSitter.supervisor.redNotify.markdownDescription: Whether a **Red** (blocked destructive action) also sends a one-way alert. The block itself always holds until you explicitly unblock.

sessionSitter.supervisor.notifyRuleDecis.markdownDescription:
Whether decisions taken by your **deterministic** `sessionSitter.autoRespond` rules are also reported to the messaging channel as one-way updates. They are always recorded and shown in the panel's Supervision activity feed; turn this off to keep them out of Telegram.

With this on, every intervention Session Sitter makes is visible — not just the ones the supervisor AI decided.

sessionSitter.dataRepoPath.markdownDescription: Absolute path to your corpus repository — the one containing `data/sessions/` (uploaded sessions) and `data/knowledge/` (the BDI tier files). Used by **Upload Session to Corpus** and, unless overridden, as the knowledge source for supervision.

sessionSitter.knowledge.registryPath.markdownDescription: Optional path to a knowledge **registry** markdown file. When set, the `(user, project, team)` triple is validated against its tables and the documented fallbacks apply (a user on exactly one project may omit the project; an unknown slug is an error). When empty, the three slugs above are used as given. See `knowledge/REGISTRY.example.md`.

sessionSitter.supervisor.knowledgeRepo.markdownDescription: Git URL of the knowledge (BDI) repository. Used only when no local checkout is configured — see `sessionSitter.dataRepoPath`.

sessionSitter.supervisor.knowledgeRef.markdownDescription: Git ref to read the knowledge repository at, when fetching it by URL.

sessionSitter.debugCommands.markdownDescription:
Show the developer commands — **Probe …**, **Install … Hook**, **Capture …** and **Test … Send** — in the Command Palette.

They exist to inspect the agent bridges by hand (which panels Claude has open, what a pending approval looks like, whether a send reaches a session) and they print to the Session Sitter output channel rather than doing anything a user asked for. Off by default so typing "Session" in the palette lists the commands you actually use. Turning this on changes nothing but their visibility.
